note: Ps102 'A prayer of one afflicted, when faint' (28v). Passages: hear my prayer v1-2; the affliction - days like smoke, heart withered, groaning, taunted, ashes and tears, God's indignation v3-11; but you are enthroned forever, you will have pity on Zion, the nations will fear, the destitute's prayer regarded v12-22; my strength broken, days cut short, but you endure, your servants' children dwell secure v23-28. IB: the AFFLICTED/FAINT one's COMPLAINT/PRAYER/CRY, the CALL; days PASS-AWAY, HEART WITHERED, FORGET to eat, GROANING, TAUNTED/DERIDED, TEARS, WITHER-AWAY; the servants who HOLD Zion dear + PITY her dust; nations FEAR; the DESTITUTE's PRAYER (x2) regarded; the vow to PRAISE/DECLARE/WORSHIP; the prisoners' GROANS. God's hear/incline/pity/favor/build-Zion/regard/endure = qualifiers; smoke/owl/sparrow/ashes/garment imagery = standalone.

dims.v: v1: 'A prayer of one AFFLICTED (ani), when he is faint' - the sufferer whose whole prayer rises from affliction.
v1: 'when he is FAINT (ataph) and pours out his complaint' - the swooning weakness from which the lament pours.
paired with the prayer and cry
v1: 'and pours out his COMPLAINT (siach) before the LORD' - the outpoured lament, grief laid before God.
v1: 'Hear my PRAYER (tephillah), O LORD' - the petition begging God's ear.
v1: 'let my CRY (shava) come to you!' - the loud plea reaching for God.
paired with the plea for a speedy answer
v2: 'in the day when I CALL (qara), answer me speedily!' - the urgent calling in the day of distress.
v3: 'For my days PASS AWAY (kalah) like smoke' - the vanishing of life, days dissolving like smoke in the affliction.
v4: 'My HEART (leb) is struck down like grass and has withered' - the inner self blighted by grief, the heart dried up.
v4: 'like grass and has WITHERED (yabesh)' - the drying-up of the heart, vitality gone in the affliction.
v4: 'I FORGET (shakach) to eat my bread' - the loss of appetite in deep grief, affliction that consumes even hunger.
v5: 'Because of my loud GROANING (anachah) my bones cling to my flesh' - the constant groaning of the sufferer, grief worn into the body.
v8: 'All the day my enemies TAUNT (charaph) me' - the ceaseless reproach the sufferer endures from his foes.
v8: 'those who DERIDE (halal) me use my name for a curse' - the sufferer's name become a byword, mockery at its cruelest.
v9: 'and mingle TEARS (beki) with my drink' - the weeping that fills the sufferer's cup, grief drunk with the water.
v11: 'I WITHER AWAY (yabesh) like grass' - the fading of the sufferer, life drying up like cut grass.
v14: 'For your servants HOLD (ratsah) her stones dear' - the love of God's people for Zion, affection even for her rubble.
paired with holding her stones dear
v14: 'and have PITY (chanan) on her dust' - the tender regard of the servants for ruined Zion, love for her very dust.
paired with the kings fearing his glory
v15: 'Nations will FEAR (yare) the name of the LORD' - the reverence the rebuilt Zion draws from the nations, awe of God's name.
v17: 'He regards the PRAYER (tephillah) of the destitute' - the prayer of the stripped-bare, which God does not overlook.
v17: 'He regards the prayer of the DESTITUTE (arar)' - the utterly poor, whose very destitution God honours with regard.
v17: 'and does not despise their PRAYER (tephillah)' - the prayer of the poor that God will not scorn.
a people yet to be created
v18: 'so that a people yet to be created may PRAISE (halal) the LORD' - the praise of generations to come, worship recorded for the future.
v20: 'to hear the GROANS (enqah) of the prisoners' - the sighing of the captives that God stoops to hear.
paired with his praise in Jerusalem
v21: 'that they may DECLARE (saphar) in Zion the name of the LORD' - the proclaiming of God's name by the freed, testimony in Zion.
v21: 'and in Jerusalem his PRAISE (tehillah)' - the praise of God rising from the restored city.
paired with the gathering of peoples
v22: 'and kingdoms, to WORSHIP (abad) the LORD' - the nations gathering to serve God, worship widened to all peoples.
v1: 'HEAR (shama) my prayer, O LORD' - God's hearing petitioned. Qualifier.
v2: 'Do not HIDE (sathar) your face from me' - God's hidden face, asked to be turned. Qualifier.
v2: 'INCLINE (natah) your ear to me' - God's attention petitioned. Qualifier.
v2: 'ANSWER (anah) me speedily!' - God's answer petitioned. Qualifier.
v2: 'answer me SPEEDILY (maher)' - God's swift response petitioned. Qualifier.
v10: 'because of your INDIGNATION (zaam) and anger' - God's displeasure. Qualifier.
v10: 'your indignation and ANGER (qetseph)' - God's wrath. Qualifier.
v10: 'for you have taken me UP (nasa)' - God's raising, then casting down. Qualifier.
v10: 'and thrown me DOWN (shalak)' - God's casting down. Qualifier.
v12: 'But you, O LORD, are enthroned FOREVER (olam)' - God's eternity. Qualifier.
v12: 'you are REMEMBERED (zeker) throughout all generations' - God's enduring renown. Qualifier.
v13: 'You will ARISE (qum) and have pity on Zion' - God's rising to act. Qualifier.
v13: 'and have PITY (racham) on Zion' - God's compassion on Zion. Qualifier.
v13: 'it is the time to FAVOUR (chanan) her' - God's favour to Zion. Qualifier.
v15: 'Nations will fear the NAME (shem) of the LORD' - God's name. Qualifier.
v15: 'and all the kings of the earth your GLORY (kabod)' - God's glory. Qualifier.
v16: 'For the LORD BUILDS UP (banah) Zion' - God's rebuilding of Zion. Qualifier.
v16: 'he APPEARS (raah) in his glory' - God's manifestation. Qualifier.
v16: 'he appears in his GLORY (kabod)' - God's glory. Qualifier.
v17: 'He REGARDS (panah) the prayer of the destitute' - God's attention to the poor. Qualifier.
v17: 'and does not DESPISE (bazah) their prayer' - God's non-contempt for the poor's prayer. Qualifier.
v18: 'Let this be RECORDED (kathab) for a generation to come' - God's word set down for the future. Qualifier.
v18: 'so that a people yet to be CREATED (bara)' - God's creating of a future people. Qualifier.
v19: 'For he LOOKED DOWN (shaqaph) from his holy height' - God's looking from heaven. Qualifier.
v19: 'from his HOLY (qodesh) height' - God's holy height. Qualifier.
v19: 'the LORD LOOKED (nabat) from heaven to the earth' - God's regard. Qualifier.
v20: 'to HEAR (shama) the groans of the prisoners' - God's hearing of the captives. Qualifier.
v20: 'to SET FREE (pathach) those who were doomed to die' - God's liberation. Qualifier.
v21: 'declare in Zion the NAME (shem) of the LORD' - God's name. Qualifier.
v22: 'when peoples GATHER (qabats) together' - the gathering of the nations to God. Qualifier.
v23: 'He has BROKEN (anah) my strength in midway' - God's breaking of the sufferer's strength. Qualifier.
v23: 'he has SHORTENED (qatsar) my days' - God's cutting short of life. Qualifier.
v26: 'They will perish, but you will REMAIN (amad)' - God's permanence. Qualifier.
v26: 'you will CHANGE (chalaph) them like a robe' - God's changing of the heavens. Qualifier.
v27: 'you are the same, and your years have no END (tamam)' - God's unchanging eternity. Qualifier.
v28: 'The children of your servants shall DWELL SECURE (shakan)' - God's securing of his servants' children. Qualifier.
